title: Karnak Temple Complex
source: Retained identity;ordinary inspected aerial pictures;standard viewer PMTiles/Mapzen terrain.
axis: +X approximately east-southeast along Amun main axis;+Yup;+Z approximately south-southwest. Native entrance is-X. Signed26°rotation is an approximation from separately mapped pylon edges,not the archaeological relation rectangle.
identityStatus: Q522862/relation14358790 is retained as archaeological identity only,never a single extruded building. Separate standard PMTiles controls identify the authored Amun core and its eastern pylon fragments,shrines,open court,exterior walls,Akhmenu ranges and exterior east temples. Mapped room/ruin containers are not blindly filled as complete roofs. Named information points are labels,not building centers. The sacred lake water is a component of PMTiles water multipolygon260831100,with a separate named point35184398171942. Southern pylon controls52776575486412–415 are independent multipart footprints;their centers and orientation are not the whole archaeological relation axis. Three independent mapped controls35184487873041,35184697656739 and35185622410047 set Khonsu,Opet and Bab El Amara. Their different axes are preserved;nearby service containers remain independent. The distant information point is not used as the temple center. Ptah uses its own six-vertex building35184462531641 and narrow eastward axis. Lakeside Taharqa35184490263836 is a named map point only;its28x20m extent and facing remain estimates with10m horizontal uncertainty. Nearby building35185932659984 remains independent. Twelve independent building controls identify the northern/entrance chapels and multipart peristyle. Named Montu35184462531640 is point-derived:90x70m extent and facing are estimates with25m horizontal/20degree angular uncertainty. No whole archaeological area is extruded. Mut ruins label35184848706149 and northern gate35185621169302 constrain the principal temple;the broad site label is not a building center. Independent mapped35184521847296 sets RamessesIII. TempleA and ChapelB remain picture-positioned estimated envelopes. Two overlapping Mut water components are unioned without altering the separate Amun lake component. Small building35185621169303 remains independent.

orientationControl.basis: Near-parallel first/second/third pylon wings and long north court wall in standard PMTiles;ordinary aerial pictures distinguish west entrance and taller southern first wing. Local pylon edges vary by about1–3degrees;not survey precision.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Only the northern SethosII shrine has a5m mapped height in these controls. Other heights, pylon batter and broken tops, columns/capitals, surviving beams, stairs and small forms are picture-guided medium-fi estimates. The side-column rhythm is an authored134-column approximation (12tall central and122smaller), not a surveyed placement or a claim of exact surviving stone count. No ancient complete roof reconstruction, copied reliefs, inscriptions or interior rooms. Two standing obelisks are visible in the retained ordinary aerial pictures. The retained PMTiles has no separate named point for them. Positions within the mapped third/fourth-pylon courts,widths and heights are picture-guided estimates;not surveyed or independently measured. Akhmenu has an authored20-column central festival-hall rhythm and separate outer piers;exact surviving counts,roof coverage,room heights and statue forms remain picture-guided approximations. No reliefs,inscriptions or historical paint are copied. Southern pylon heights and broken profiles are inferred from ordinary aerial views;the PMTiles supplies their footprint pairs,not surveyed heights. Lake depth,water level,bank width and stair sections are visualization estimates. Coarse statue/Scarab silhouettes do not reproduce fine historical carving. Khonsu and Opet heights,roof survival,upper apertures,cornices,column rhythm,raised entrance and Bab El Amara dimensions are inferred from ordinary exterior pictures. Shared stone textures supply broad material character;no reliefs or lettering are copied. Ptah portal heights,gate stations,partial roof survival and columns,and Taharqa low enclosure,pit depths,internal pockets and stairs are picture-guided medium-fi estimates. No reliefs,inscriptions or hidden historical interiors are reproduced. Northern shrine,piers,cornices,beams,ramps and broken ruin heights are picture-guided estimates. Hakoris alone has a mapped5m height;its open pavilion arrangement is typological. White/alabaster and red-stone tints reuse the same material graphs. Hidden rooms,carving,inscriptions and hypothetical complete ancient roofs are omitted. Mut surviving low ruins,broken porch columns,door jambs and representative statue forms use ordinary photographs. Heights,room survival,statue counts and small features are estimated. Complete ancient roofs,sculpture detail,reliefs and lettering are omitted.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Unchanged retained standard161-square/16m viewer DEM. Geographic vertical poses use local DEM medians;processional and approach ramps join the independent floor groups. Native-water lower quartiles set both lake levels. The257-square/6m source-local review fixture lowers only occupied pockets for isolated inspection;separate actual-site captures use the unmodified DEM. Approximate visualization fit,not surveyed archaeological grades or hydrology.
reconstruction.scope: Principal medium-fi exterior visualization of Karnak:Amun entrance,courts,hypostyle hall,eastern pylons/obelisks,shrines,Akhmenu,east temples,sacred lake,southern pylons,Khonsu,Opet,Bab El Amara,Ptah,Taharqa,northern/entrance chapels,peristyle,Montu and Mut precinct exteriors. Fine carving,inscriptions,exact ruin inventories and hidden historic interiors are omitted. Point-derived Montu,Taharqa,main Mut,TempleA and ChapelB retain explicit uncertainty. Standard-map/DEM site fit is approximate.

east.source: Separate mapped wall,building and building_part polygons from retained standard Protomaps20261014;ordinary aerial pictures. Overlapping Wadjethall parts are controls for open ruins,not whole roofs.
east.obeliskBasis: Two standing obelisks are visible in the retained ordinary aerial pictures. The retained PMTiles has no separate named point for them. Positions within the mapped third/fourth-pylon courts,widths and heights are picture-guided estimates;not surveyed or independently measured.
east.geometryBasis: Mapped multipart fourth/fifth/sixth pylon fragments,central Bark/Kamutef shrines,open Middle Kingdom courtyard,long exterior wall runs,Akhmenu festival hall and separate chamber/range footprints,Contra,RamessesII and eastern Taharqa colonnade. Walls follow their own runs;open courts and collapsed roof areas stay open. Heights,capitals,beam survival,room partitions and broken silhouettes are coarse exterior estimates. Generic cell-pattern remains in the open court are explicitly reconstructed,not mapped building footprints.

lake.basis: Full lake-water ring retained from standard PMTiles multipolygon,with its small shoreline recesses. Five-meter outer bank and six inferred stairs are authored approximations;levels are not measured hydrology. Static opaque water is a visualization surface;actual host terrain/water integration remains pending.

south.geometryBasis: Four separate multipart southern pylon footprints set the positions,span,thickness and slightly different axes. Broken heights,batter,door lintel,connecting court walls,statue silhouettes,Scarab dimensions and Amenhotep II wall remains are picture-guided medium-fi estimates. Inter-pylon ground stays open. Modern independent service buildings and vegetation are not part of this authored component.

west.geometryBasis: Three independent standard PMTiles footprints control Khonsu,Opet and Bab El Amara. Khonsu opens south toward the gateway;Opet has a separate east-west axis and western entrance. Twin battered pylons,upper apertures,open court,colonnades,stepped rear roofs,lower Opet range,raised narrow entrance and the freestanding portal are picture-guided estimates. Heights,exact roof survival,court-column rhythm,stair and lintel dimensions are not measured. Neighbor35185622410052 and nearby service buildings are ambiguous independent features and are not absorbed into these temples. Information point17605653873171 is not a temple anchor.

ptah.geometryBasis: Separate six-vertex PMTiles footprint sets the narrow approach and widened eastern temple range. Four axial portals,open approach courts,low interrupted walls,a partial portico roof and separate rear sanctuary/side-chapel masses are picture-guided approximations. Heights,exact gate stations,column count and surviving roof coverage are not surveyed.

taharqa.geometryBasis: The retained standard map provides a named point,not an independently identified building polygon.28x20m extent and the main-temple-aligned facing are explicit picture-guided estimates around that point. Low outer masonry,three open below-grade pockets,broken internal walls and a narrow descending approach represent the surviving remnant;no hypothetical full temple roof. Neighbor35185932659984 remains a separate mapped building.

ptahTaharqa.source: Retained standard PMTiles/Mapzen extract and ordinary exterior pictures only;no bespoke survey or terrain download.

ruins.name: Chapel of Osiris Wennefer Neb djefau

peristyle.geometryBasis: Two independent multipart reconstruction envelopes retain their original floor outlines. Paired square-pier rows and selected beam strips follow the long envelope directions. Court gaps remain open. Counts,post stations and exact surviving beams are picture-guided approximations.

montu.geometryBasis: Standard PMTiles supplies a named precinct point but no identified temple footprint in this extract.90x70m extent and north-south local axis are explicit estimates with25m horizontal and20degree angular uncertainty. Ordinary exterior picture guides low open court walls,three separate jamb remnants and low column stubs. No complete ancient temple or unobserved tall gateway is reconstructed. The precinct remains geographic-review pending.

north.geometryBasis: Independent mapped shrine and multipart peristyle footprints are kept distinct. White Chapel uses raised open piers and opposing access flights;Red Chapel has dark base,red stone side walls and open axial portals. Other alabaster shrines use the pictured barque-shrine family;Osiris,Imperial Cult and Hatshepsut remain coarse open shells. Hakoris has its mapped5m height with an estimated open pavilion arrangement. Heights,roof survival,paint,sculpture and exact pillar/fragment inventories are not surveyed. Material tints reuse shared stone graphs;no copied artwork.

main.geometryBasis: Actual ruins label35184848706149,independent northern gate and crescent-lake peninsula constrain this inferred tapered temple envelope. Broad archaeological label35184490244501 lies at the rear lake and is not a building center. Surviving low walls,open courts and broken porch-column rhythms follow ordinary photographs;room partitions,stations and heights are medium-fi estimates,not a measured reconstruction.

ramessesIII.geometryBasis: Independent mapped building envelope sets long axis and scale. Aerial identifies the southwest RamessesIII temple. Open court,low broken walls,room ranges and column remnants are picture-guided estimates;no complete ancient roof.

templeA.geometryBasis: No identified PMTiles building polygon in this extract. Ordinary aerial positions the low east-west temple east of the Mut entrance. Extent,axis and room layout are explicit estimates;do not treat it as independently mapped geometry.

chapelB.geometryBasis: Small open low ruin east of lake in ordinary aerial. Point and envelope are estimates,not a mapped footprint.

lake.name: Isheru crescent lake
lake.geometryBasis: Union only the two overlapping Mut water components,not every component of multipolygon260831100,which also contains the separate Amun lake. Concave crescent preserves the central dry peninsula. Bank width,basin depth and water level are authored visualization estimates,not measured hydrology.

mut.geometryBasis: Three distinct temple ranges,northern gateway and small ChapelB remain separate open ruins. Reuse existing shared stone graphs and linear tints. Coarse statue silhouettes are representative,not an inventory or copied sculpture. No blanket roof or whole-precinct slab.

buildingMask.basis: Independent building-only masks for 52 mapped authored controls,with a 3 cm outward allowance for numerical edge slivers. Every independent retained building and inner courtyard hole is preserved,with a 2 mm numerical guard;these allowances are not surveyed precision. Masks with holes are partitioned into simple pieces;no synthetic connectors,whole-precinct extrusion or archaeological-relation replacement.

integrationControls.groundBasis: 31 separate occupied floor and basin pockets derived from the intersection of upward source surfaces present at every resident LOD. Intervening site terrain is retained. This defines coverage,not surveyed archaeological grades;final actual-DEM seating review remains pending.
integrationControls.waterBasis: Only the mapped Amun sacred-lake and Isheru crescent footprints. Other components and independent water features sharing an ID stay intact. Ground and water replacement are separately bounded and follow resident model pieces;native water returns on unload or failed loading.

integrationGrades.basis: Existing unmodified standard viewer DEM only. Independent temple/shrine groups receive rigid vertical poses from neighborhood medians;the processional courts follow a piecewise linear grade. Lake levels follow the native-water interior lower-quartile rule plus its normal0.65m offset. These are approximate visualization grades,not surveyed floors or hydrology. Intrinsic detailed recipes remain unchanged and buildKarnakUnposed reconstructs their pre-fit master.

montu.basis: Low separate ruin fragments follow the retained DEM,so estimated walls are not buried by a whole-precinct flat plane.

south.basis: Piecewise linear processional grade connecting the retained DEM neighborhood medians. Floor grades and broken-wall poses are visualization estimates. The first court ties to the Amun threshold;following stations use the retained neighborhood medians.

integrationReview.basis: Approximate exterior placement from retained standard viewer PMTiles and unmodified161-square/16m DEM plus ordinary pictures. The hypostyle-hall control anchors the signed26-degree axis;native+X points ESE,+Z SSW,+Y up. NativeY0 is the DEM sample at the exact model anchor. Independent temple/shrine groups use retained-DEM neighborhood medians;processional and approach ramps connect their levels. Both lake levels use retained native-water lower quartiles. Thirty-one covered ground pockets and52separate building masks preserve432independent retained building records. Actual DEM tile:365independent records unchanged. Native-water replacement is limited to the two modeled lake footprints;failed loads,partial residency and eviction preserve or restore unloaded surfaces. Architectural grades and point-derived envelopes/facing remain visualization estimates,not surveyed archaeological elevations or hydrology.
